item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02380","case1_error":"Uses the old monthly salary for all 41 new-company months, omitting the 20% raise.","case2_error":"Treats the extra day's 50% premium as its entire pay, omitting the base daily wage.","reason":"Case 1 omits the increase while retaining base pay; case 2 retains the increase while omitting base pay.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02381","case1_error":"Calculates new-company earnings at the old salary, ignoring the 20% raise.","case2_error":"Counts the original 24 brownies again when adding the new batch to the 12 remaining brownies.","reason":"The first omits a required salary adjustment; the second double-counts the original batch.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02382","case1_error":"Leading answer marker says 600, but the correct derivation and conclusion give 400 legs.","case2_error":"Leading answer marker says 16, but the correct derivation and conclusion give 8 students.","reason":"Both contain only answer-marker conflicts with otherwise correct mathematics, requiring an uncertain judgment.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02383","case1_error":"Inserts an unsupported $3,000 tax expense; 20% of the $5,000 pretax profit is $1,000.","case2_error":"Provides unsupported final numbers after correct weekly-pay formulas, which yield $675.","reason":"The first introduces an incorrect intermediate expense without a calculation; the second appends incorrect final numbers to correct formulas.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02384","case1_error":"Answer marker says $300, while the explanation correctly calculates $200 remaining.","case2_error":"Appends unsupported final answer 68 after the correct formula 40 + (0.20 × 40), which yields 48.","reason":"Case 1 has only an answer-marker conflict, so a comparison of mathematical error mechanisms is uncertain.","judgment":"uncertain"}]}
